opportunity: On every big-endian 32-bit ABI a two-register value comes back with the HIGH word in the first register (PowerPC r3, MIPS o32 $2, SPARC %o0, ARM BE r0; AArch64 BE x0 for __int128), and AVR's gcc ABI returns an int with the high byte in R25, the first register of its reversesignif join rule. Return recovery and the call-output pair joined that register as the low half, so clang -O2 `long long wide_mul(int,int)` printed `CONCAT44(a1 * a0,(int)(... >> 0x20))` on PowerPC, MIPS, SPARC and ARM big-endian, and AVR `int negate(int)` printed `CONCAT11(a1,a0)`.

change_kind: strict correctness fix (no option: it only changes register-pair returns and call outputs whose output rule joins the first register high -- every big-endian target, and AVR's gcc spec through reversesignif; every other target is byte-identical)
inspiration: upstream FuncCallSpecs::buildOutputFromTrials reads ParamActive::isJoinReverse; ActionReturnRecovery::buildReturnOutput does not
root_cause: buildReturnOutput and kuna_rustabi::build_call_output_pair took trial 0 (the first register in storage order) as the low half. The <join/> output rule records whether it consumed the most significant piece first (MultiSlotAssign::consumeMostSig -> ParamActive::setJoinReverse): by default on a big-endian register space, and flipped by reversesignif (AVR's gcc spec, little-endian, sets it), and nothing read it at the return. With the halves in the rule's order, more defects showed. SPARC's restore copies %i1 back to %o1 on every return, so %o1 reaches the RETURN holding whatever the function left in %i1 (the incoming argument, clang -O0's scratch zero, an unrelocated sethi pair, or a value zero at the exit), and the rule pool folds a zero half out of the join (PIECE(ZEXT(x),y) -> ZEXT(PIECE(x,y)), PIECE(0,y) -> ZEXT(y), PIECE(x,0) -> ZEXT(x) << 32) before the uncomputed-half repair runs; the swapped order had narrowed many of these to %o0 by accident. SPARC's call pcode also keeps a RETURN for a delay-slot restore that didrestore = 0 never reaches, where %o1 is the call's argument. And AVR maps its registers into data memory, so the contiguous pair's parent register R25R24 is a global that merged with the argument bytes and printed as `return R25R24;`.
fix: ParamActive::join_pair_order decides which trial is the low half; build_return_output and build_call_output_pair use it. kuna_rustabi::pair_join_address keeps a join record when the contiguous pair's parent register is global storage (AVR). After the join every decision reads the order back from storage: kuna_returnuncomputed::first_register_holds_high (the high half sits in the earlier model output entry, ParamListStandard::holds_high_first), used by the late repair (look through ZEXT(PIECE(x,lo)), first-in-class tie-break, one-register guard) and holds_scalar_pair. classify_window_pair (return recovery, pair joined first register high, kept on Funcdata::kuna_window_pair): HandedBack when a register-window move (moves_register_window: one instruction copying every general-purpose argument register, SPARC save/restore, either end possibly a heritage temporary) defines the second register at every live RETURN; Leftover when it also holds its entry value or a literal (built_from_literals) there through copies/indirects/phis, every register-moving copy a window's; RETURNs behind branches literals decide the other way are skipped (never_reached). The pair is always built. zero_leftover_low_half (right after the join and at the start of every later pass): a Leftover's PIECE low input becomes zero where the high input is zero, so PIECE(0, a1) folds into a literal instead of ZEXT(a1). The late repair keeps a Leftover pair's first register from the PIECE (a literal second register counts as leftover), and for any window pair reads ZEXT(x) << lo (shifted_high_half: keep x) and a literal (literal_pair: keep a new constant of its high half, stored in the first register, window_high_storage). narrow_window_pair (every pass) gives each RETURN SUBPIECE(whole, lo) in the first register only when some RETURN has a shape the late repair does not read (late_strippable) and the register is a Leftover or the low half is zero at every RETURN (low_bits_zero). The first version asked only for the entry value and printed ARM BE `unsigned long long f(unsigned a,unsigned b){ext();return b;}` (mov r4,r1; bl ext; mov r1,r4) as `return 0`; the second dropped only the untouched argument and turned 49 functions main printed narrow (by accident) into `x << 32`; three intermediate versions of this round narrowed during the main loop more widely or zeroed every leftover, which made a single %o0 return one variable with the first argument through SPARC's unrelocated calls (SQLite `a0 = (struct_100 *)0x1; return a0;`, +192 `a0 =` lines) or typed GH-6990's return uint4 Round 4 (review: a restore destination write counted as the window's, and every literal in %i1 as scratch): moves_register_window accepts only a COPY of one register into another (the register possibly a heritage PIECE of its pieces), so `restore %g0,1,%o1` (tmp = 0 + 1; %o1 = tmp) is the function's own write (WindowPair::No). window_values walks %i1 back through window copies, phis and indirects, then PIECE/SUBPIECE, to entry values, literals and values; a literal that reaches the first register's slot (unchanged, or through any op but a sign extension) unless all ones, and a computed value copied unchanged there with its top bit clear, are set aside; a RETURN with every path set aside holds a leftover; the rest are followed forward: reaching only RETURNs is deliberate (No), a literal reaching a store/call/branch/load address is a leftover, a used value is handed back. Any deliberate RETURN -> No; else any leftover -> Leftover; else HandedBack. The late repair repairs a window pair at every live RETURN or none and repoints every RETURN before destroying concatenations. clear_dead_varnodes now takes a freed Varnode out of its HighVariable (C++ ~Varnode): with a window pair repaired at every RETURN, an input left unread after merging stayed in its variable and the naming pass read it (SQLite replaceFunc panicked).
